perspective:
From Harold Padilla’s available perspective:

- He is a project manager dealing with a project whose progress is suffering.
- He feels frustrated and anxious, and believes his team is unmotivated.
- He knows Arthur as a friend/police officer he trusts for advice, and arranged a coffee-shop meeting with him.
- He told Arthur his team seemed unmotivated and he was at his wit’s end.
- He heard Arthur say motivation can be tricky, suggest understanding what drives each team member, and recommend one-on-one conversations to make people feel valued and understood personally.
- Harold said he had not done that and would try it; afterward he felt hopeful and relieved.
- He told his team he wanted one-on-one chats to understand what motivates them and said he would schedule time with each person.
- He heard Team Member 1 say that could be helpful and Team Member 2 say they were open to it.
- Later, Harold noticed the team still was not responding well. He felt disappointed and worried about the project’s future.
- He told Arthur he had tried the suggestions but the team still wasn’t responding. Arthur suggested there might be deeper issues such as personal conflicts, lack of trust, or external stressors.
- Harold said he hadn’t thought of that, would set up another round of meetings, and thanked Arthur.
- Harold then held one-on-one meetings and asked team members to share concerns or problems.
- He heard Team Member 1 say there was tension between a few people affecting work.
- He heard Team Member 2 say they felt overwhelmed by the workload and stressed, making motivation hard.
- Harold said he would look into resolving conflicts and would see about redistributing tasks to ease pressure, and said their well-being was important.
- Harold felt optimistic and empowered, believing addressing individual concerns would improve performance.
- He told the team he would implement regular feedback sessions and team-building activities to create a more supportive environment.
- He heard Team Member 1 say that sounded great and would help, and Team Member 2 agree that their concerns were being addressed.
- Harold said he was glad and that their input and well-being were crucial to the project’s success.

Harold does not have access to any hidden events, private thoughts, or unspoken information beyond what he personally experienced, observed, was told, or did.
